newsitem.title: UK: GKN extends gains, litigation fear overdone.
newsitem.headline: GKN extends gains, litigation fear overdone.

text.p: Shares in engineering group GKN Plc extended gains late Friday morning after an unsteady start, which was prompted by a U.S. court decision to award a record $601 million in damages against the company.
The shares dropped to lows of 950p in pre-market trade soon after the decision was announced. But the stock had recovered to be up 38-1/2p to 10.12-1/2 stg by 1030 GMT.
"We have to look at the level the shares have risen from," said Andy Chambers, industry analyst at SocGen.
"The price has been absolutely trashed by various press comments in recent weeks, indicating that they could have up to $800 million of liability."
The shares reached a peak of 11.73 stg in October last year but in the last four months they have fallen 22 percent to a low of 9.14 stg in February.

"The market was over-discounting the worst case scenario," Chambers said. "We now have a clear figure of the provision and likely cash outflow from the litigation and we can ascertain what the real impact on earnings is likely to be."

The U.S. district court's judgement ended a four year litigation against GKN's U.S. exhaust retailer, Meineke Discount Mufflers. The record damages were awarded against the company for misusing advertising fees and defrauding franchisees. But GKN has said it intends to appeal the decision. "I think they have a very good chance of getting the damages substantially reduced from this level or even completely overturned," the analyst said. "We already know that the initial award will be reduced by 34 percent anyway."
